ov: Birds of prey that scavenge carrion. The 16 Old World vultures of Europe, Africa and Asia and the 7 New World vultures and condors of the Americas look alike but aren’t closely related.
rg: Old World vultures: Europe, Africa and Asia. New World vultures and condors: North and South America.
df: Carrion. The bearded vulture is the only vertebrate that specialises in eating bones.

cf.tip: Many vultures have a bare, unfeathered head that stays clean while they feed on carcasses. Eagles mostly hunt live prey.

fx: Some New World vultures find carcasses by smell; Old World vultures use only sight.
A group of vultures in flight is a “kettle”, and a feeding group is a “wake”.
